independentReview.head: 91a4b15a078390e55de1c9ce4e6afff416e8a423
independentReview.reason: TWO APPROVES at this exact head after TWO REQUEST CHANGES at the previous one, and the round-1 refusals are recorded rather than smoothed over because they are what makes this approval worth anything. ROUND 1, head 77b7605b: both reviewers refused. Finding 1 - the unit test at scripts/handoff-worktree-truth.test.mjs:716-717, labelled in its own comment as proving the #243 shape where 'the grace is spent', asserted .toBe(true) using a stub hand-tuned to agree with that wrong expectation and inverted against the real isAncestorOrEqual; a reviewer proved it by flipping the assertion to .toBe(false), which FAILED against the shipped code, and the orchestrator confirmed it independently against the source. The production logic was correct; the evidence for it was not, which is issue #322's lens exactly. Finding 2, the material one - the grace was keyed on the branch TIP, and a reviewer demonstrated in a scratch repository that when a landing merge must conflict-resolve docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md the merge commit itself becomes the freshest editor of that path and is an ancestor of NEITHER parent, so grace was denied and #333 reproduced unchanged. That is the case that actually recurs, this file being the repo's documented merge hotspot, so round 1 survived its own merge on timing rather than on mechanism. Finding 3 - commit 0b555277's message asserted the inverted behaviour as fact. ROUND 2, this head: a fresh writer added landingCommitOf/landingCommitOnMain, resolving the landing commit as the oldest entry of git rev-list --ancestry-path <tip>..origin/main with a fallback to the tip, and rewired rules A and D to ask about the LANDING rather than the raw tip; replaced the inverted stub with one derived from an explicit descendant map in the real parent-to-child direction; and corrected 0b555277's false claim in 795e6eaa's message, in the guard's header comment and in the PR body, since amend and rebase are barred. THE GAP THE WRITER DISCLOSED ITSELF was made the reviewers' first task: landingCommitOnMain was exercised only through injected stubs, so what git rev-list --ancestry-path actually returns, and in what order, was an assumption no shipped test could falsify. Reviewer A closed it by measurement rather than argument - built scratch git repositories outside every checkout, imported this PR's own exported functions, and confirmed --ancestry-path prints newest-first across single-entry, empty and five-entry topologies so the oldest-entry selection resolves the immediate landing and never a later one; then ran the whole decision end to end on real SHAs for a clean merge (freshest editor is the branch's own commit under history simplification, landing is the merge commit, graced), for a conflict-resolving merge (freshest editor IS the merge commit, landing equals it, graced by equality - the exact case round 1 failed), and for the stale case (advancing main past both landings with later doc-touching commits returns not-graced for both). It also ran round-1 and round-2 logic side by side on identical real data: false then true. Reviewer B audited for weakening and found every failure mode degrades toward DENYING grace - an empty ancestry path falls back to the tip, which is correct because both call sites only ask isGraced after already confirming the branch landed; an unresolvable ref short-circuits to not-graced; unreadable history returns not-graced immediately; and landingCommitOnMain throwing reverts to round 1's stricter behaviour, never to an open pass. B also verified the second commit was load-bearing by checking out 795e6eaa alone and watching the disposition audit fail without it, and checked every factual claim in both new commit messages, the PR body, the guard's new header paragraphs and the new disposition row, including the thirty-six ref count against git ls-remote and the reflow against git diff --word-diff=plain. ONE NON-BLOCKING GAP, named by both reviewers and accepted rather than hidden: the 2026-09-01 narrowing of rule C (#312) shipped a live quantified before-and-after on this machine, and this narrowing ships no equivalent measurement of how many currently-named branches sit inside the grace window. Both reviewers judged that a documentation-thoroughness gap rather than a correctness one, and both judged this narrowing principled rather than convenience-driven, on the ground that rule C and rules A/D were not merely inconvenient together but unsatisfiable together, empirically at commit 5b1e3f9c. Two narrowings of one guard file in two days is recorded here as a pattern worth watching, since both were argued for rather than slipped in, and the next narrowing should meet #312's quantified bar.
